paragraphs.text: But there arose false prophets also among the people, as among you also there shall be false teachers, who shall privily bring in destructive heresies, denying even the Master that bought them, bringing upon themselves swift destruction.
paragraphs.original: Ἐγένοντο δὲ καὶ ψευδοπροφῆται ἐν τῷ λαῷ, ὡς καὶ ἐν ὑμῖν ἔσονται ψευδοδιδάσκαλοι, οἵτινες παρεισάξουσιν αἱρέσεις ἀπωλείας, καὶ τὸν ἀγοράσαντα αὐτοὺς δεσπότην ἀρνούμενοι, ἐπάγοντες ἑαυτοῖς ταχινὴν ἀπώλειαν·
paragraphs.translit: Egenonto de kai pseudoprophētai en tō laō, hōs kai en hymin esontai pseudodidaskaloi, hoitines pareisaxousin haireseis apōleias, kai ton agorasanta autous despotēn arnoumenoi, epagontes heautois tachinēn apōleian·

paragraphs.text: And many shall follow their lascivious doings; by reason of whom the way of the truth shall be evil spoken of.
paragraphs.original: καὶ πολλοὶ ἐξακολουθήσουσιν αὐτῶν ταῖς ἀσελγείαις, διʼ οὓς ἡ ὁδὸς τῆς ἀληθείας βλασφημηθήσεται·
paragraphs.translit: kai polloi exakolouthēsousin autōn tais aselgeiais, diʼ hous hē hodos tēs alētheias blasphēmēthēsetai·

paragraphs.text: And in covetousness shall they with feigned words make merchandise of you: whose sentence now from of old lingereth not, and their destruction slumbereth not.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἐν πλεονεξίᾳ πλαστοῖς λόγοις ὑμᾶς ἐμπορεύσονται· οἷς τὸ κρίμα ἔκπαλαι οὐκ ἀργεῖ, καὶ ἡ ἀπώλεια αὐτῶν οὐ νυστάζει.
paragraphs.translit: kai en pleonexia plastois logois hymas emporeusontai· hois to krima ekpalai ouk argei, kai hē apōleia autōn ou nystazei.

paragraphs.text: For if God spared not angels when they sinned, but cast them down to hell, and committed them to pits of darkness, to be reserved unto judgment;
paragraphs.original: Εἰ γὰρ ὁ θεὸς ἀγγέλων ἁμαρτησάντων οὐκ ἐφείσατο, ἀλλὰ σειραῖς ζόφου ταρταρώσας παρέδωκεν εἰς κρίσιν τηρουμένους,
paragraphs.translit: Ei gar ho theos angelōn hamartēsantōn ouk epheisato, alla seirais zophou tartarōsas paredōken eis krisin tēroumenous,

paragraphs.text: and spared not the ancient world, but preserved Noah with seven others, a preacher of righteousness, when he brought a flood upon the world of the ungodly;
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἀρχαίου κόσμου οὐκ ἐφείσατο, ἀλλὰ ὄγδοον Νῶε δικαιοσύνης κήρυκα ἐφύλαξεν, κατακλυσμὸν κόσμῳ ἀσεβῶν ἐπάξας,
paragraphs.translit: kai archaiou kosmou ouk epheisato, alla ogdoon Nōe dikaiosynēs kēryka ephylaxen, kataklysmon kosmō asebōn epaxas,

paragraphs.text: and turning the cities of Sodom and Gomorrah into ashes condemned them with an overthrow, having made them an example unto those that should live ungodly;
paragraphs.original: καὶ πόλεις Σοδόμων καὶ Γομόρρας τεφρώσας καταστροφῇ κατέκρινεν, ὑπόδειγμα μελλόντων ἀσεβέσιν τεθεικώς,
paragraphs.translit: kai poleis Sodomōn kai Gomorras tephrōsas katastrophē katekrinen, hypodeigma mellontōn asebesin tetheikōs,

paragraphs.text: and delivered righteous Lot, sore distressed by the lascivious life of the wicked
paragraphs.original: καὶ δίκαιον Λὼτ καταπονούμενον ὑπὸ τῆς τῶν ἀθέσμων ἐν ἀσελγείᾳ ἀναστροφῆς ἐρρύσατο—
paragraphs.translit: kai dikaion Lōt kataponoumenon hypo tēs tōn athesmōn en aselgeia anastrophēs errysato—

paragraphs.text: (for that righteous man dwelling among them, in seeing and hearing, vexed [his] righteous soul from day to day with [their] lawless deeds):
paragraphs.original: βλέμματι γὰρ καὶ ἀκοῇ ὁ δίκαιος ἐγκατοικῶν ἐν αὐτοῖς ἡμέραν ἐξ ἡμέρας ψυχὴν δικαίαν ἀνόμοις ἔργοις ἐβασάνιζεν—
paragraphs.translit: blemmati gar kai akoē ho dikaios enkatoikōn en autois hēmeran ex hēmeras psychēn dikaian anomois ergois ebasanizen—

paragraphs.text: the Lord knoweth how to deliver the godly out of temptation, and to keep the unrighteous under punishment unto the day of judgment;
paragraphs.original: οἶδεν κύριος εὐσεβεῖς ἐκ πειρασμοῦ ῥύεσθαι, ἀδίκους δὲ εἰς ἡμέραν κρίσεως κολαζομένους τηρεῖν,
paragraphs.translit: oiden kyrios eusebeis ek peirasmou rhyesthai, adikous de eis hēmeran kriseōs kolazomenous tērein,

paragraphs.text: but chiefly them that walk after the flesh in the lust of defilement, and despise dominion. Daring, self-willed, they tremble not to rail at dignities:
paragraphs.original: μάλιστα δὲ τοὺς ὀπίσω σαρκὸς ἐν ἐπιθυμίᾳ μιασμοῦ πορευομένους καὶ κυριότητος καταφρονοῦντας. Τολμηταί, αὐθάδεις, δόξας οὐ τρέμουσιν, βλασφημοῦντες,
paragraphs.translit: malista de tous opisō sarkos en epithymia miasmou poreuomenous kai kyriotētos kataphronountas. Tolmētai, authadeis, doxas ou tremousin, blasphēmountes,

paragraphs.text: whereas angels, though greater in might and power, bring not a railing judgment against them before the Lord.
paragraphs.original: ὅπου ἄγγελοι ἰσχύϊ καὶ δυνάμει μείζονες ὄντες οὐ φέρουσιν κατʼ αὐτῶν βλάσφημον κρίσιν.
paragraphs.translit: hopou angeloi ischyi kai dynamei meizones ontes ou pherousin katʼ autōn blasphēmon krisin.

paragraphs.text: But these, as creatures without reason, born mere animals to be taken and destroyed, railing in matters whereof they are ignorant, shall in their destroying surely be destroyed,
paragraphs.original: οὗτοι δέ, ὡς ἄλογα ζῷα γεγεννημένα φυσικὰ εἰς ἅλωσιν καὶ φθοράν, ἐν οἷς ἀγνοοῦσιν βλασφημοῦντες, ἐν τῇ φθορᾷ αὐτῶν καὶ φθαρήσονται,
paragraphs.translit: houtoi de, hōs aloga zōa gegennēmena physika eis halōsin kai phthoran, en hois agnoousin blasphēmountes, en tē phthora autōn kai phtharēsontai,

paragraphs.text: suffering wrong as the hire of wrong-doing; [men] that count it pleasure to revel in the day-time, spots and blemishes, revelling in their deceivings while they feast with you;
paragraphs.original: ἀδικούμενοι μισθὸν ἀδικίας· ἡδονὴν ἡγούμενοι τὴν ἐν ἡμέρᾳ τρυφήν, σπίλοι καὶ μῶμοι ἐντρυφῶντες ἐν ταῖς ἀπάταις αὐτῶν συνευωχούμενοι ὑμῖν,
paragraphs.translit: adikoumenoi misthon adikias· hēdonēn hēgoumenoi tēn en hēmera tryphēn, spiloi kai mōmoi entryphōntes en tais apatais autōn syneuōchoumenoi hymin,

paragraphs.text: having eyes full of adultery, and that cannot cease from sin; enticing unstedfast souls; having a heart exercised in covetousness; children of cursing;
paragraphs.original: ὀφθαλμοὺς ἔχοντες μεστοὺς μοιχαλίδος καὶ ἀκαταπαύστους ἁμαρτίας, δελεάζοντες ψυχὰς ἀστηρίκτους, καρδίαν γεγυμνασμένην πλεονεξίας ἔχοντες, κατάρας τέκνα,
paragraphs.translit: ophthalmous echontes mestous moichalidos kai akatapaustous hamartias, deleazontes psychas astēriktous, kardian gegymnasmenēn pleonexias echontes, kataras tekna,

paragraphs.text: forsaking the right way, they went astray, having followed the way of Balaam the [son] of Beor, who loved the hire of wrong-doing;
paragraphs.original: καταλιπόντες εὐθεῖαν ὁδὸν ἐπλανήθησαν, ἐξακολουθήσαντες τῇ ὁδῷ τοῦ Βαλαὰμ τοῦ Βοσὸρ ὃς μισθὸν ἀδικίας ἠγάπησεν
paragraphs.translit: katalipontes eutheian hodon eplanēthēsan, exakolouthēsantes tē hodō tou Balaam tou Bosor hos misthon adikias ēgapēsen

paragraphs.text: but he was rebuked for his own transgression: a dumb ass spake with man`s voice and stayed the madness of the prophet.
paragraphs.original: ἔλεγξιν δὲ ἔσχεν ἰδίας παρανομίας· ὑποζύγιον ἄφωνον ἐν ἀνθρώπου φωνῇ φθεγξάμενον ἐκώλυσεν τὴν τοῦ προφήτου παραφρονίαν.
paragraphs.translit: elenxin de eschen idias paranomias· hypozygion aphōnon en anthrōpou phōnē phthenxamenon ekōlysen tēn tou prophētou paraphronian.

paragraphs.text: These are springs without water, and mists driven by a storm; for whom the blackness of darkness hath been reserved.
paragraphs.original: Οὗτοί εἰσιν πηγαὶ ἄνυδροι καὶ ὁμίχλαι ὑπὸ λαίλαπος ἐλαυνόμεναι, οἷς ὁ ζόφος τοῦ σκότους τετήρηται.
paragraphs.translit: Houtoi eisin pēgai anydroi kai homichlai hypo lailapos elaunomenai, hois ho zophos tou skotous tetērētai.

paragraphs.text: For, uttering great swelling [words] of vanity, they entice in the lusts of the flesh, by lasciviousness, those who are just escaping from them that live in error;
paragraphs.original: ὑπέρογκα γὰρ ματαιότητος φθεγγόμενοι δελεάζουσιν ἐν ἐπιθυμίαις σαρκὸς ἀσελγείαις τοὺς ὀλίγως ἀποφεύγοντας τοὺς ἐν πλάνῃ ἀναστρεφομένους,
paragraphs.translit: hyperonka gar mataiotētos phthengomenoi deleazousin en epithymiais sarkos aselgeiais tous oligōs apopheugontas tous en planē anastrephomenous,

paragraphs.text: promising them liberty, while they themselves are bondservants of corruption; for of whom a man is overcome, of the same is he also brought into bondage.
paragraphs.original: ἐλευθερίαν αὐτοῖς ἐπαγγελλόμενοι, αὐτοὶ δοῦλοι ὑπάρχοντες τῆς φθορᾶς· ᾧ γάρ τις ἥττηται, τούτῳ καὶ δεδούλωται.
paragraphs.translit: eleutherian autois epangellomenoi, autoi douloi hyparchontes tēs phthoras· hō gar tis hēttētai, toutō kai dedoulōtai.

paragraphs.text: For if, after they have escaped the defilements of the world through the knowledge of the Lord and Saviour Jesus Christ, they are again entangled therein and overcome, the last state is become worse with them than the first.
paragraphs.original: εἰ γὰρ ἀποφυγόντες τὰ μιάσματα τοῦ κόσμου ἐν ἐπιγνώσει τοῦ κυρίου καὶ σωτῆρος Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ τούτοις δὲ πάλιν ἐμπλακέντες ἡττῶνται, γέγονεν αὐτοῖς τὰ ἔσχατα χείρονα τῶν πρώτων.
paragraphs.translit: ei gar apophygontes ta miasmata tou kosmou en epignōsei tou kyriou kai sōtēros Iēsou Christou toutois de palin emplakentes hēttōntai, gegonen autois ta eschata cheirona tōn prōtōn.

paragraphs.text: For it were better for them not to have known the way of righteousness, than, after knowing it, to turn back from the holy commandment delivered unto them.
paragraphs.original: κρεῖττον γὰρ ἦν αὐτοῖς μὴ ἐπεγνωκέναι τὴν ὁδὸν τῆς δικαιοσύνης ἢ ἐπιγνοῦσιν ὑποστρέψαι ἐκ τῆς παραδοθείσης αὐτοῖς ἁγίας ἐντολῆς·
paragraphs.translit: kreitton gar ēn autois mē epegnōkenai tēn hodon tēs dikaiosynēs ē epignousin hypostrepsai ek tēs paradotheisēs autois hagias entolēs·

paragraphs.text: It has happened unto them according to the true proverb, The dog turning to his own vomit again, and the sow that had washed to wallowing in the mire.
paragraphs.original: συμβέβηκεν αὐτοῖς τὸ τῆς ἀληθοῦς παροιμίας· Κύων ἐπιστρέψας ἐπὶ τὸ ἴδιον ἐξέραμα, καί· Ὗς λουσαμένη εἰς κυλισμὸν βορβόρου.
paragraphs.translit: symbebēken autois to tēs alēthous paroimias· Kyōn epistrepsas epi to idion exerama, kai· Hys lousamenē eis kylismon borborou.
